analysis:
Changes reviewed:
1) coordinator/api/routes.go head lines 291-292 add GET /v1/admin/autopilot/machines and PATCH /v1/admin/autopilot/machines/{machine_id}, both wrapped only in s.access.RequireAuth and routed to handleAdminAutopilotMachines. This matches the existing autopilot admin routes at lines 289-290 and 293. RequireAuth accepts any consumer API key or Privy JWT, so the real admin gate (isAdminAuthorized/requireAdminKey) must be inside the handler. The handler source was not supplied, so ownership/admin enforcement and PATCH input validation (machine_id scoping, mutable fields) are unverified. This is a coverage limit (T-004, TB-006), not a finding. The next pass should confirm that the handler rejects non-admin callers for both methods and cannot cross accounts.
2) middleware.go head line 121 adds PATCH to Access-Control-Allow-Methods. It is only in the credentialed single-origin branch (CORS_ORIGIN, default console.darkbloom.dev); the public wildcard branch stays GET/OPTIONS. This is not a regression, but it makes PATCH preflights succeed from the console origin. It also affects the existing PATCH /v1/keys/{id}, which already requires RequirePrivyAuth (TB-004).
3) autopilotcontrol/controller.go adds a monotonic evaluationTime epoch, so queueing and IO delay are counted against freshness and a buffered ticker timestamp cannot extend it. It also adds a shadow planning pass on a cloned fleet. Shadow actions only call ports.Propose and do not touch live Reserve/Send, and limit is zeroed when paused or ledger-not-ready. Live passes now run with ObserveOnly set to limit=0. No authorization, attestation or encryption interaction was seen; this is operational scheduling only. Summary.Proposed is now LiveProposed+ShadowProposed, so downstream consumers or UI may misread it, which is a correctness point, not a security one.
No new findings. Deeper review is only needed for the unseen handleAdminAutopilotMachines.
